title: Deepfake Scams
about: Spot a faked voice or video, and check who's really there.

cards.situation: Unknown number. It sounds exactly like Grandma, and she needs money.

image.alt: A call on your phone from an unknown number, 12 seconds in. A sound wave, then the caller's words in bubbles: It's Grandma! I've lost my purse. Send me $200 now. Don't tell your parents.

cards.prompt: A scammer copies 5 seconds of Grandma's voice from a video. **What can they make?**

image.alt: Left, a social post: Grandma blowing out birthday candles, a 5-second video. An arrow points to a scammer at a laptop on the right.
image.revealAlt: The scammer's laptop now plays a sound wave in Grandma's voice, saying words she never said: I've lost my purse. Send me $200 now.

options.text: Her voice, saying anything they type
Only that same clip, word for word
Nothing: it takes hours of recordings

cards.explanation: AI learns how Grandma sounds from a short clip, then makes her voice say new things.

cards.title: Deepfakes
cards.body:
A voice, face or video faked with AI is a **deepfake**. Warning signs: an unknown number, a rush for money, and a secret.

A voice you know proves nothing, so hang up and call the number you already have.

image.alt: The call from an unknown number, its voice tagged: Could be a deepfake. Beside the phone, a contact card: Grandma, saved in your phone, tagged: Call this one.

cards.prompt: You've hung up. Now check it was really Grandma. **Tap how you check.**

image.alt: Your phone after the call, with three big buttons: Call back Unknown number. Call Grandma (saved). Text Unknown number: Is it you?
image.revealAlt: Call Grandma (saved) is lit. The real Grandma answers at home: My purse? It's right here!

options.nudge: Which number belongs to the real Grandma, not the caller?

options.text: Text Unknown number: Is it you?
options.nudge: Which number belongs to the real Grandma, not the caller?

cards.explanation: Yes: her saved number reaches the real Grandma, and the scammer can't answer it.
cards.showAnswer: Call Grandma's saved number: the unknown number belongs to the caller, who'd just answer again.

cards.prompt: Next day, a video call. Grandma's face asks for $200, right now. **Tap what you do.**

image.alt: A video call from an unknown number. Grandma's face fills the screen and a bubble says: Quick, love, send it now!
image.revealAlt: The video call has ended. You call Grandma's saved number: she answers at home with a puzzled smile and says: Hello love! What video call?

options.text: Hang up and call her saved number
Send it: I can see her face
options.nudge: Faces can be copied, just like voices. What can't a scammer fake?

options.text: Ask for another video to prove it
options.nudge: Faces can be copied, just like voices. What can't a scammer fake?

cards.explanation: Right: faces can be faked too, but a deepfake can't answer Grandma's real phone.
cards.showAnswer: Hang up and call her saved number: a deepfake can make another video, but it can't answer her real phone.

cards.prompt: A video message from an account with your coach's face. **Tap what you do.**

image.alt: A chat from an account named Coach, with a round picture of a person in a cap with a whistle. A video message shows the same face. Under it: Send me a photo of you in your uniform. Keep it between us.

options.text: Don't reply; tell a trusted adult

options.nudge: Look past the face. Which warning sign is in the message itself?
Look past the face. Which warning sign is in the message itself?

cards.explanation: Yes: "Keep it between us" is a warning sign, whatever the face, and a trusted adult can check.
cards.showAnswer: Don't reply, and tell a trusted adult: real or fake, a secret photo request is a warning sign.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
A voice or face you know can be faked: hang up and check on the number you already have, or ask a trusted adult.

**Try this:** Agree a secret family word with your family tonight, to check calls like this.

**Next:** Something mean online: what to save before you block.
